intent: The clickable header that expands or collapses its AccordionItem.
typical_uses: The single header/summary child of an AccordionItem

dont_use_when.situation: A standalone button with no AccordionItem to expand or collapse

invariants.text: AccordionTrigger always renders a trailing chevron that rotates on open/close - there is no prop to hide it, matching upstream Base UI.

anti_patterns.dont: Pass an icon element through children expecting it before the chevron
anti_patterns.do_instead: Children are the trigger's text label only; the chevron is fixed and always trailing

a11y.by: Base UI's Accordion.Header and Accordion.Trigger - focus handling and the aria-expanded/aria-controls wiring

render.states: render replaces the trigger element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the trigger's state; neither is expressible in JSON Schema. The trailing chevron is rendered as a child, so it survives a replaced element.

style.states: style accepts a function of the trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`; a JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form.

unexposed_parts.reason: The kit's AccordionTrigger composes Base UI's Accordion.Header (a plain wrapper, not separately exposed by the kit) around Accordion.Trigger into one exported component; this contract describes the exported surface, not the two-part internal composition, so Header's own props are not part of it.

good.title: A trigger as an AccordionItem's header

bad.title: A trigger with no AccordionItem around it
bad.why: AccordionTrigger reads and writes the nearest AccordionItem's open state through Base UI context; outside one, clicking it does nothing.
